newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian demand seen reviving on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian demand seen reviving on uncertainty.

text.p: A political crisis looming large over India may push up demand for gold and its prices in the country, analysts and dealers said on Monday.
They said the withdrawal of support by the Congress Party to India's 13-party United Front (UF) coalition government had pushed the country to the brink of a deep political crisis.
"Normally demand for precious metals emerges during a crisis," said bullion analyst Madhusudan Daga. "But it is too premature to predict what is likely to happen."
Daga said an anticipated revival of wedding season demand for gold from mid-April would also help keep prices firm.
"In any case, prices will not go down," he said.

Congress president Sitaram Kesri's surprise decision on Sunday to withdraw support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minirity government prompted political confusion that sent share prices tumbling.
"The money from stock markets need not necessarily come into bullion at this stage," Daga said.
However, dealers feel the political crisis may not have much impact on bullion markets.
"Some government will be formed. And no government will go back on the economic reforms," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
India has in the last few years allowed imports of gold and silver subject to customs duties.
"Gold prices will rise only if the Indian rupee becomes weak against the dollar because of the political developments," Damani said.
On Monday the Indian rupee held steady at 35.91/92 per dollar after a brief pause when it lost 10 paise to 35.99 per dollar.
On the Bombay bullion market on Monday, standard gold opened 35 rupees per 10 grammes higher at 4,715 rupees, though it lost 15 rupees per 10 grammes over the week.
"I expect prices to remain firm," Damani said.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, dealers said gold prices were down because of low demand from jewellers.
In the week to Saturday, gold prices fell 43 Pakistan rupees per 10 grammes to 4,706 Pakistan rupees.
Dealers in Dubai said they expected retail trade to get a boost from a month-long shopping festival in the Gulf emirates city that began on Thursday.
Backers of the festival and its parallel "Dubai city of gold" promotion, expect some two million visitors to come to Dubai in April attracted by bargain jewellery, gold coins, ingots and bars.
"With a large number of visitors from India, jewellery (demand) will go higher," a Dubai-based gold wholesaler said.
